ak-gov-2026-bronson-dave.name: Dave Bronson
ak-gov-2026-bronson-dave.bio: Former mayor of Anchorage and U.S. Air Force pilot.

positions.stance: Develop Alaska's natural resources, including oil, gas, mining, critical minerals and timber, to create jobs and strengthen state finances "without raising taxes."
Invest in roads, bridges and ports so businesses can thrive and families can prosper.
"Secure control of Alaska's land and put it to work for families, ensuring housing is attainable and communities can grow."
End "bloated bureaucracy and political agendas in schools"; focus on reading, writing and math; reward great teachers; and restore parents' rights.
Says the PFD "belongs to the people of Alaska" and supports a full statutory PFD.

ak-gov-2026-kreiss-tomkins-jonathan.name: Jonathan S. "JKT" Kreiss-Tomkins
ak-gov-2026-kreiss-tomkins-jonathan.bio: Former state legislator who represented Southeast Alaska for a decade.

positions.stance: Fully fund schools, pass a constitutional amendment to "forward fund" education, pay teachers fairly and create a defined benefit retirement system.
Support development of all energy sources and require the four Railbelt utilities to cooperate to provide cheaper electricity.
Protect Medicaid expansion, promote telehealth, expand in-home care for seniors and outlaw excessive drug price markups.
Rein in bottom trawl bycatch, keep commercial fishing permits in Alaska and prioritize restoring crashed Chinook runs.
Supports a moratorium on new data centers until comprehensive regulation passes, and holding AI companies liable in Alaska courts when products cause harm.

ak-gov-2026-taylor-treg.name: Treg Taylor
ak-gov-2026-taylor-treg.bio: Former Alaska Attorney General (2021-2025) and Deputy Attorney General; attorney and small-business owner.

positions.stance: Will "unleash Alaska's energy potential, making energy affordable for every Alaskan family."
Cut red tape and reform permitting to attract investment, grow small businesses and create higher-paying jobs.
Pledges an emphasis on "accountability, problem-solving, and putting Alaskans first" to end budget stalemates in Juneau.
Will fight rising costs for fuel, housing and everyday goods "so Alaskans can afford to live and thrive in Alaska."
Will "fight to keep costs down for Alaska families" as food prices rise.

ak-gov-2026-wilson-bernadette.name: Bernadette M. Wilson
ak-gov-2026-wilson-bernadette.bio: Has served as CEO of the Alaska Policy Forum and in leadership at Americans for Prosperity.

positions.stance: Calls for transparency and accountability in education funding and says Educational Savings Accounts and backpack funding should be seriously considered.
Says the PFD is a dividend owed to Alaskans under the statutory formula and the governor must ensure the law is followed: "We own our resources. Follow the law."

vt-gov-2026-janoo-amanda.name: Amanda Janoo
vt-gov-2026-janoo-amanda.bio: Has worked for nearly two decades with governments and communities in the U.S. and abroad on economic strategy.

positions.stance: Strengthen Vermont's economy "from the bottom up" by investing in local businesses, farmers, workers and cooperatives, including creating a Vermont Public Bank.
Invest in permanently affordable housing and ask corporate investors, second homes and commercial vacation rentals to contribute more, to lower housing costs and property taxes.
Protect and invest in public schools as community hubs "instead of consolidating our public schools out of existence."
Calls for banning AI data centers and regulating Big Tech so Vermonters control their data and privacy.
Make primary care free and universal, emphasizing preventive medicine, as a foundation for a universal healthcare system.

vt-gov-2026-scott-phil.name: Phil Scott
vt-gov-2026-scott-phil.bio: Governor of Vermont; former lieutenant governor, five-term state senator and construction company co-owner.

positions.stance: Running "to lead Vermont forward, build a stronger economy"; says he is focused on growing the economy.
Running to "make Vermont more affordable."
Says he is focused on "protecting the most vulnerable."

vt-ltgov-2026-gray-molly.name: Molly Gray
vt-ltgov-2026-gray-molly.bio: Former Lieutenant Governor of Vermont who later led the Vermont Afghan Alliance.

positions.stance: Supports "universal primary care for every Vermonter."
"Urgently build more affordable housing."
"Protect every Vermonter against unlawful and unconstitutional federal actions."
"Fight for Vermont's rural communities."

vt-ltgov-2026-rodgers-john.name: John S. Rodgers
vt-ltgov-2026-rodgers-john.bio: Lieutenant Governor of Vermont since 2024; former state representative and state senator, farmer and small-business owner.

positions.stance: Committed to lowering costs by opposing unnecessary taxes, mandates and government spending that burden families, seniors, farmers and small businesses.
Will stand up for property rights and traditional land uses and oppose policies that make it harder for farmers, loggers and landowners to make a living.
Supports reducing unnecessary regulations, encouraging investment and helping small businesses grow.
Supports practical reforms that make it easier to build homes and modernize outdated regulations while preserving Vermont's community character.
Strong advocate for career and technical education, apprenticeships and workforce development programs.

wy-gov-2026-barlow-eric.name: Eric Barlow
wy-gov-2026-barlow-eric.bio: U.S. Marine Corps veteran, large-animal veterinarian and rancher; former Wyoming House Speaker who later served in the State Senate.

positions.stance: Protect freedom and state sovereignty and "live within our means, including cash-based budgeting."
Strengthen minerals and energy, tourism, agriculture and small businesses, and encourage innovation and investment in new technologies and manufacturing.
Ensure communities retain local control and have critical needs met, including safety, education, healthcare and infrastructure.
Says property rights are "the backbone of Wyoming's freedom"; supports landowner rights and strong water rights laws.
Supports policies that strengthen rural communities and values local volunteers and nonprofits.

vt-gov-2026-roy-dean.name: Dean Roy
vt-gov-2026-roy-dean.bio: Stowe native and former Vermont legislative page who founded the Freedom and Unity Party in 2025.

positions.stance: Promises "no new restrictions on any freedoms," including digital freedoms, firearm rights, LGBT+ rights, minority rights and the right to abortion.
Wants to raise taxes on short-term rental room revenue to cut taxes for Vermont's middle and lower class.
Supports a public option for those earning under $100,000, funded by higher taxes on the wealthiest, and an eventual move to universal healthcare.
Opposes the state's electric vehicle mandate as restricting personal autonomy and "a clear example of government overreach."
Supports scrapping Act 250, saying it restricts housing permitting and adds building costs.

wy-gov-2026-bextel-rebecca.name: Rebecca Bextel
wy-gov-2026-bextel-rebecca.bio: Small-business owner who has lived in Wyoming for more than 20 years.

positions.stance: "Our rights come from God. Government exists to protect them, not grant them"; pledges to veto bills that infringe on freedoms.
Would withdraw Wyoming from federal refugee resettlement and end any policy letting illegal immigrants obtain Wyoming driver's licenses.
Will defend Wyoming energy workers and producers "against radical green agendas" and politically motivated regulations.
Opposes gun-control mandates, firearm registries and red-flag laws that deny due process.
Will fight for "meaningful, permanent property-tax reform," including limits on excessive assessment increases.

H2CA50026.name: Juan Vargas
H2CA50026.bio: U.S. Representative for California's 52nd District since 2012; former state senator, assemblymember, San Diego city councilmember and attorney.

positions.stance: Working to grow good-paying jobs through clean energy and infrastructure investment and support for small businesses.
Committed to expanding affordable healthcare, lowering prescription drug costs, ensuring mental health care and protecting veterans' benefits.
Fights for fair funding, affordable college, before- and after-school programs, and excellent public education for every child.
Advocates pathways to citizenship, protections for Dreamers, and "humane immigration policies that keep families together."
Pushes for policies that protect LGBTQIA+ communities and defend equality under the law.

H6CA52163.name: Jeff Belle
H6CA52163.bio: U.S. Navy veteran, private equity CEO and former elected official.

positions.stance: Supports increasing housing supply, speeding approvals and making it easier to build starter homes, apartments near transit and affordable units.
Supports stronger border security, tougher action against cartels and smugglers, and a lawful, swift immigration process that works for employers and families.
Will fight for fairer federal funding formulas so more dollars reach San Diego-area classrooms, "not bureaucracy."
Work to reduce red tape, improve access to capital and support workforce and apprenticeship programs.

H2TX01112.name: Nathaniel Moran
H2TX01112.bio: U.S. Representative for East Texas since 2023; former Smith County Judge and attorney.

H6TX01352.name: Yolanda Prince
H6TX01352.bio: Project manager at Prairie View A&M University's Texas Juvenile Crime Prevention Center and business owner.

positions.stance: Congress must lower everyday costs; will work to make homeownership more attainable for first-time buyers and middle-class families.
Supports raising the federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour.
Supports raising teacher pay, expanding special education, universal school meals and universal pre-kindergarten.
Congress must increase Medicare reimbursement rates to keep rural healthcare facilities open.
Supports "a Medicare for All single-payer healthcare system" guaranteeing coverage for every American.

H6TX02251.name: Shaun Finnie
H6TX02251.bio: Former oil and gas lawyer with 30 years in energy investment banking.

positions.stance: "Ensure all Texans can afford to live and work here."
"Remove the Tariffs."
"Address the federal debt to protect the economic futures of our young people."
Protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid benefits of middle-class Americans "from any potential cuts."
"Ensure that women have the right to make their own healthcare decisions."

H6TX08175.name: Steve Toth
H6TX08175.bio: Ordained pastor, small-business owner and Texas state representative.

positions.stance: Won't stop fighting until Congress acts to keep Americans safe from "human traffickers, cartels, and dangerous criminals" crossing the southern border.
Says "radical liberal ideology doesn't belong in our classrooms"; led efforts to eliminate CRT and DEI in Texas schools.
Will work for "peace through strength," defend allies like Israel, and ensure foreign spending serves Americans' interests.
Will protect the right to self-defense; says red flag laws and other unlawful restrictions "have no place in America."
Committed to giving law enforcement the resources they need to succeed.

H6TX03234.name: Evan Hunt
H6TX03234.bio: Retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and defense and aerospace industry executive.

positions.stance: Will stand up for free and fair elections, an independent judiciary, checks and balances, and the peaceful transfer of power.
Says people should be treated with dignity and respect regardless of immigration status, race, religion or orientation.
Supports a public-private partnership for an affordable baseline, lower drug prices, eliminating wasteful middlemen and more healthcare transparency.
Supports fully funding public schools and merit-informed teacher pay increases; "firmly against voucher initiatives."
Supports border security, streamlined legal immigration and a path for law-abiding immigrants, plus "efficient deportations of undocumented criminals."

H2TX00064.name: Keith Self
H2TX00064.bio: U.S. Representative and retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel; former Collin County Judge (2006-2018).

positions.stance: Supports resuming border wall construction, Operation Lone Star, and federal reimbursement to Texas for its border security efforts.
Will keep working to "lower taxes, cut wasteful spending and reduce the size of government."
Founded the Sharia-Free America Caucus to stop the growing influence of Sharia in Texas and America.
Working to stop Green New Deal policies and expand refining capacity and exploration toward energy independence.
Believes elections must remain under state control; supports photo ID to vote and paper trails on voting machines.

H0TX04219.name: Pat Fallon
H0TX04219.bio: Congressman; former Texas state senator, state representative and city council member, military veteran and business owner.

H6TX04174.name: Jason Pearce
H6TX04174.bio: Former mortgage-industry sales professional who later worked in finance and insurance.

positions.stance: "Medicare for All."
"Housing is a human right."
"Work should pay."
"I answer to you. Not donors."
"Expand Social Security. Don't cut it."

H6TX05189.name: Chelsey Hockett
H6TX05189.bio: Mother of two and community organizer from Terrell, Texas.

positions.stance: Will fight to "End Trump's Tariffs."
Supports enacting Medicare for All to eliminate health insurance premiums and deductibles.
Supports universal childcare "so parents can afford to raise their kids and participate in the workforce."
Tie the minimum wage to cost of living, "starting with a $25 Minimum Wage."
Tie benefits to cost of living, starting with a $200 increase, funded by removing the cap on the Social Security tax.

H8TX06266.name: Jake Ellzey
H8TX06266.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 6th District, retired Navy fighter pilot and commercial airline pilot; former Texas Veterans Commission commissioner.

positions.stance: "I'm a proud gun owner and lifetime member of the NRA"; pledges to defend the Second Amendment.
"I 100% support the right to life as the first and most vital right."
Pass legislation to secure the border, finish the wall and give Border Patrol agents the resources they need.
Opposes "land grab projects" like the proposed high-speed rail that would destroy farmland.
Will stand up against "job-killing regulations" that serve big businesses and special interests.
"Healthcare is a right, not a luxury"; supports universal, affordable healthcare.
"Raise wages. Lower costs. Put working families first."
Supports a stronger Department of Education and making school vouchers illegal nationwide.
Will fight to require a congressional vote before troops are sent into lasting conflicts and to set time limits on military action.
Supports a secure, well-managed border, civil immigration enforcement, and ending family separation and mass detention camps.

H8TX07140.name: Lizzie Fletcher
H8TX07140.bio: U.S. Representative for Texas's 7th District; former business litigation attorney and law firm partner.

positions.stance: Supports improving the Addicks and Barker Reservoirs, coastal surge protection, revised floodplain maps and on-time federal flood projects.
Calls improving infrastructure for the growing Houston region "one of my top priorities" and seeks Houston's fair share of federal transportation dollars.
Supports trade with key partners, vocational and retraining programs, and eliminating the gender wage gap.
